_comment: THE ZERO-REGRESSION OBJECT BASELINE, RE-TAKEN FROM THE TREE THE BACKFILL ACTUALLY PUBLISHED.
The zero-regression plan states three acceptance numbers and records
that one of them — 138,287 objects — was `reported, record not located`, with the
instruction to re-take it before the refactor rather than carry it forward. This file is
that reading. It is NOT a re-run: the genesis-to-tip publish of 2026-09-10 left its tree
on disk beside its ledger, and this is a measurement of that tree, so it is the baseline
itself rather than a reconstruction of one.
THE REPORTED NUMBER WAS RIGHT, AND IT WAS NOT UNRECORDED EITHER. The tree holds exactly
138,287 objects. The figure was already written down at `tools/chain/ingest-range.mjs`
line 549 — as a sentence in a comment, which is why a search for a measurement record
found nothing. A comment is not a baseline: nothing can be compared against it.
A COUNT IS NOT A BASELINE EITHER, WHICH IS WHY THE DIGESTS ARE THE POINT. The plan's own
control says a tree with one object renamed has the same count and must fail. `pathDigest`
and `setDigest` are what fails; `tools/chain/object-set-selftest.mjs` R2 is that exact
control, and R4 is the harder one — two objects swapping contents, where the count, the
byte total and the key set are all identical.
THE FULL MANIFEST IS NOT COMMITTED: it is 22.7 MB, 10.7 MB compressed. The per-class
digests below are the affordable substitute — a difference localises to an object class
without a re-run. Getting the individual objects needs `--manifest` on both trees.
objects = blocks + 3 x transactions + 6, on the metadata-only path. 75,971 + 3 x 20,770
+ 6 = 138,287, and the class table below is that identity term by term. The three
per-transaction objects are `tx` (immutable facts), `ts` (the TraceSelection overlay) and
`g/{gen}/txstate`, all three written for every transaction including private-only, pruned
and refused ones. The six singletons are `registry/chains.v1.json`, `current.json`, and
the generation's `root.json`, `summary.json`, `height/0.json` and `blocks/0.json`.
measures: the published tree written by the genesis-to-tip metadata backfill of 2026-09-10

provenance.kind: a tree left on disk by the run that produced it, not a re-publish
provenance.branch: bt/backfill-full (head 77b1d59), landed on dev in eac2c12

ledger.reVerifiedBy: node tools/chain/coverage-contiguity.mjs <ledger> 1 75971 -> CONTIGUOUS WITH ZERO GAPS: YES, notServed 0, throttledOut 0

caveats: THE PUBLISHING TREE WAS DIRTY. `lastPublishedCodeVersion` records commit 7fc17cc with
`dirty: true`, so the bytes that produced this tree are not exactly any commit. The
working tree evidently already carried the fix that landed as fd3d275 — `current.json`
here says `finalized.height: 75971`, and the defect fd3d275 fixes is a whole-history
publish writing `finalized: {height: 1}`. A post-refactor comparison against this
reading is therefore against a tree built from 7fc17cc-plus-uncommitted, not from a
nameable commit, and a difference traceable to those uncommitted bytes is a difference
to be explained rather than a regression.
THE STATE DIRECTORY IS MACHINE-LOCAL and `.gitignore`d. This reading is committed
precisely because the tree it measures is not, and will not survive the machine.
THIS IS THE METADATA-ONLY PATH: `tracesPublished` is 0, so no `t/**` trace objects,
no `src/**` source bundles and no `/idx/**` are in this set. A post-refactor run that
publishes traces is measuring a different thing and the counts are not comparable.
